momentum-conservation-s1.title: Cart A hits cart B
momentum-conservation-s1.html: The track is level and friction is negligible. Positive is to the right.

momentum-conservation-s2.title: A dart and a block
momentum-conservation-s2.html: The dart sticks in the block. Use g = 9.8 m/s².

items.q: What is cart B's velocity after the collision, in m/s?

mistakes.why: Value: B does not simply take A's speed. Use momentum: (0.50)(0.80) = (0.50)(0.30) + (0.25)v_B.
Value: that is A's change in velocity. B's mass is half of A's, so B's change is twice as large.

why.correct: System: both carts. External forces (gravity, normal) balance and friction is negligible, so p is constant: (0.50)(0.80) = (0.50)(0.30) + (0.25)v_B, giving v_B = +1.0 m/s.

items.q: Which is the best justification for using momentum conservation here?
options: The net external force on the two carts is zero: vertical forces balance and friction is negligible
Momentum is conserved because of the law of conservation of momentum, which holds for any collision
The carts exert equal forces on each other, so each cart's momentum is constant
Kinetic energy is conserved in the collision, so momentum is conserved as well

why.correct: A system's momentum is constant when the net external force on it is zero. State the system and why the external forces add to zero.
options: Right: it names the system and the condition.
Circular: it states the law without the condition that makes it apply.
Each cart's momentum changes. The equal and opposite forces make the changes cancel in the total.
Momentum does not follow from kinetic energy; and K need not be conserved here.

items.q: How does the impulse cart A exerts on cart B compare with the impulse cart B exerts on cart A?
options: B's impulse on A is larger, because A is heavier
Equal in size and opposite in direction
A's impulse on B is larger, because B speeds up more
Equal in size and in the same direction

why.correct: Δp_A = (0.50)(0.30 − 0.80) = −0.25 kg·m/s; Δp_B = (0.25)(1.0 − 0) = +0.25 kg·m/s. Equal and opposite, so the total is unchanged.
options: Third-law forces are equal regardless of the masses.
Right: the forces are a third-law pair acting for the same time.
B's larger velocity change comes from its smaller mass, not from a larger impulse.
Third-law forces point in opposite directions.

items.q: Take cart A alone as the system. Which is correct?
options: A's momentum is constant, because the track is frictionless
A's momentum is constant, because the collision is brief
A's momentum is not constant, because B exerts an external force on it
A has no momentum after the collision, since its momentum went to B

why.correct: Whether momentum is constant depends on the system. Cart A alone feels B's external push; the two-cart system does not.
options: Friction is not the only external force. B's push on A changes A's momentum.
Brief or not, B's push gives A an impulse of −0.25 N·s.
Right: with B outside the system, B's push is external.
A still moves at 0.30 m/s, so p_A = 0.15 kg·m/s.

items.q: How does the velocity of the center of mass of the two carts after the collision compare with before?
options: It increases, because B speeds up
It decreases, because A slows down
It is zero after the collision
It is the same, about +0.53 m/s

why.correct: v_cm = (0.40 kg·m/s)/(0.75 kg) = 0.53 m/s both times. With no net external force, the center of mass keeps a constant velocity.
options: A slows down by the matching amount of momentum; the total is unchanged.
B gains exactly the momentum A loses.
The total momentum is still 0.40 kg·m/s, not zero.
Right: v_cm = Σp/Σm = 0.40/0.75 before and after.

items.q: How fast do the dart and block move just after the dart sticks, in m/s?

mistakes.why: Value: after the collision the dart moves with the block. Divide by the total mass, 0.500 kg.
Value: that sets kinetic energies equal. The dart sticks, so kinetic energy is not conserved; use momentum.

why.correct: Momentum of the dart-block system: (0.050 kg)(40 m/s) = (0.500 kg)v, so v = 4.0 m/s.

items.q: Why can momentum, but not kinetic energy, be used to find the speed just after the dart sticks?
options: No net external force acts on them, but friction inside the block makes thermal energy
Kinetic energy is conserved as well, but the momentum equation is easier to solve
Momentum is conserved just for collisions where the objects join
The rough patch removes momentum but not kinetic energy

why.correct: During the impact the only horizontal forces are internal, so p is constant. The dart tearing into the wood does negative work inside the system, so K drops from 40 J to 4.0 J.
options: Right: momentum's condition holds; mechanical energy's does not.
Kinetic energy falls from 40 J to 4.0 J; it is not conserved.
Momentum is conserved in any collision with no net external force.
The rough patch comes after the collision and removes both.

items.q: The dart and block then slide onto the rough patch. How far do they slide before stopping, in meters?

mistakes.why: Value: that uses the dart's speed. On the patch the dart and block move together at 4.0 m/s.

why.correct: Friction does work −μ_k(M)g d = 0 − ½Mv², so d = v²/(2μ_k g) = (4.0 m/s)²/(2 × 0.40 × 9.8 m/s²) = 2.0 m.

items.q: While the dart and block slide on the rough patch, is the momentum of the dart-block system constant?
options: Yes: momentum is conserved whatever the forces
No: friction from the patch is a net external force
Yes: the dart and the block move together as one object
No: the dart is now inside the block

why.correct: On the patch, friction from the floor is an unbalanced external force, so the system's momentum decreases to zero.
options: Momentum is constant only with no net external force. Friction is external here.
Right: the floor is outside the system, and its friction slows it.
Moving together does not stop an external force from changing their momentum.
Where the dart sits does not matter; the external friction does.

items.q: A ball falls toward Earth. For which system is momentum constant (ignoring the rest of the universe)?
options: The ball alone
Earth alone
Ball + Earth
Neither the ball alone nor ball + Earth

why.correct: Ball alone: Earth's pull is external, so p changes. Ball + Earth: the pull is internal, so the total momentum is constant. Earth's tiny upward speed balances the ball's.
options: Earth's pull is external to the ball and increases its downward momentum.
The ball pulls Earth up, an external force on Earth.
Right: the gravitational forces between them are internal and cancel.
With both inside, the only forces are internal; the total is constant.

items.q: A 60. kg skater at rest throws a 3.0 kg ball forward at 8.0 m/s on frictionless ice. What is the skater's recoil speed, in m/s?

mistakes.why: Value: the skater and ball separate, so the skater's mass alone (60. kg) carries the recoil.

why.correct: Starting p = 0: 0 = (3.0)(8.0) + (60.)v, so v = −0.40 m/s, a speed of 0.40 m/s backward.

items.q: An astronaut at rest throws a wrench away. If she throws a wrench of twice the mass at the same speed, her recoil speed becomes
options: 4 times as large
√2 times as large
the same
2 times as large

why.correct: m_a v_a = m_w v_w. Doubling m_w at the same v_w doubles v_a.
options: Momentum is linear in mass; nothing is squared.
That would come from equal kinetic energies, which is not the condition here.
The wrench carries twice the momentum, so she must too.
Right: her momentum must balance the wrench's, which doubles.

items.q: Two ice skaters push off each other from rest. Skater 1 has twice the mass of skater 2. Which statement is correct?
options: Skater 2 moves off twice as fast as skater 1, the other way
Both move away at the same speed, in opposite directions
Skater 1 moves away twice as fast, because skater 1 is bigger
Skater 1 does not move, because skater 2 does the pushing

why.correct: The total momentum stays zero: m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ = 0 with m₁ = 2m₂ gives v₂ = −2v₁.
options: Right: equal and opposite momenta, so the lighter skater is faster.
Equal forces give equal momenta, not equal speeds.
The heavier skater is the slower one.
Each pushes the other with equal and opposite forces (third law).

items.q: A 1.5 kg cart moving right at 2.0 m/s collides with a 0.50 kg cart moving left at 3.0 m/s. After the collision the 0.50 kg cart moves right at 1.5 m/s. What is the 1.5 kg cart's velocity after, in m/s? Include the sign (right positive).

mistakes.why: Value: the 0.50 kg cart moves left before, so its momentum is negative: (0.50)(−3.0).

items.q: A moving cart collides with a cart at rest on a level, frictionless track. For the two-cart system, compare after with before.

variables.name: The total momentum
variables.why: No net external force acts, so the total momentum is constant.

variables.name: The velocity of the center of mass
The momentum of the cart that was moving
variables.why: The other cart pushes it backward, an impulse opposite its motion.

why.correct: Internal forces move momentum between the carts but cannot change the total or the center of mass's velocity.
